summary: UNODC handbook detailing internationally recognized good practices for the establishment and operation of witness protection programmes in the context of organized crime.

measures: Withholding identity details from the public record

institutional_framework.witness_protection_authority: Decision-making body (government, police, or judicial) overseeing admission and policy.
institutional_framework.witness_protection_unit: Covert operational unit responsible for physical security and identity change.

legal_and_operational_requirements: Strict admission criteria based on case significance and psychological assessment.
Mandatory Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the witness and the authority.
Robust procedures for maintaining secrecy and penalizing unauthorized disclosures.
Mechanisms to ensure witnesses do not use new identities to evade existing civil or criminal liabilities.
international_standards: Article 24 and 26 of the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNCAC) mandate witness and cooperator protection.
